analysis:
Examined both supplied CI excerpts and the change map against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041 definition. Head .github/workflows/ci.yml:17-25 introduces push-only cache saving and sparse checkout; lines 60-93, 163-197, 226-260 and 464-498 restore/cache Git metadata. These paths use pinned actions, connectivity checks, and persist-credentials:false. The save predicate excludes pull requests, so the visible changes do not establish an attacker-controlled PR cache being published for trusted branch jobs. git fsck checks connectivity, not cache provenance or configuration safety; that distinction alone is not proof of a regression without an attacker-writable cache path.
Head lines 266 and 507 pass cache-save policy into provider-ci-build; lines 400-416 retain the pinned audio cache key while restricting saves. Shard execution, native admission/lifecycle gates, prompt parity and full-suite auditing remain present in the head excerpt (298-399, 513-519). Base lines 529-676 show nested numerical/cache safety gates; 678-893 show cluster checks and the fail-closed selected-lane gate. Their corresponding later head sections are not supplied here, so preservation cannot be concluded from this batch.
No visible change modifies prompt encryption, account-scoped cache identity, KEK custody, serving authorization, billing or privileged helper admission (A-001/A-003, T-008, T-041, T-052–T-054). Integration should examine .github/actions/provider-ci-build and cache helper changes for source/toolchain binding, trusted cache provenance and credential exclusion, and reconcile later CI changes with the base test gates. Sparse exclusion of evidence archives must also be checked against changed test consumers. These are coverage questions, not demonstrated vulnerabilities.
